question: ________ was the Governor General of India when the Permanent Settlement was introduced.
solution:
The **correct** answer is **Lord Cornwallis**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **1793,** with **Lord Cornwallis** serving as Governor-General, **Permanent **Settlement was **established**.
 
• This was put in place with the **intention** of giving the **East India** Company a **reliable source **of **income **and motivating the **zamindars** to make **improvements** to the land.
 
• Many **significant issues** were brought about by the **British East India** Company for the **people** of **India**.
 
• One of the **troublesome laws** that the British enacted was the Permanent Settlement Act of **1793**.
 
• The **British East India** Company and the **Bengali Landlords** came to an **arrangement **over the **payment **of the upcoming **land tax**.
 
• As **Governor General**, Lord Cornwallis **visited** India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lord Linlithgow**

 
 
• ​The **Government** of India **Act of 1935,** which outlined plans for **local self-government**, was put into action at **Linlithgow**.
 
• He **experienced** both his share of **successes** and the **setbacks** that most **Viceroys** have.
 
• In **pre-war India**, he was regarded as a calm, **diplomatic**, and rational **politician** who, against** Mr. Gandhi's** opposition, was able to establish regional **autonomy**.
 
 
 
• **Lord** William **Bentinck**
 
 
• **Bentinck** enlisted in the **British army** at the **age of 16**, and by 1798, he was a colonel.
 
• He was **appointed Madras**' **Governor** in 1803.
 
• From **1828 **to **1835,** he then held the position of **Governor-General of India**.
 
• While **serving** as the Governor-General of **British India**, he is **credited** with implementing reforms in the **legal, social, **and** educational **sectors.
 
 
 
• **Lord Irwin**
 
 
• **​**On **March 5, 1931,** Lord Irwin, the **Viceroy** of India, and** Mahatma Gandhi **formed a political pact known as the **Gandhi-Irwin Pact**.
 
• As a result of **Gandhi** and his supporters' **Salt March**, a period of **civil disobedience** (satyagraha) against British authority in India came to an end.
 
• To spare the **violent criminals**, it consented to the release of all **political detainees**.
 
• It consented to permit **nonviolent picketing** of liquor and foreign **clothing stores**.
 
• It **consented** to lift the **restriction** on the INC.
 
• It promised to **return** the Satyagrahis' **confiscated p**roperty.
